The test image shows a green tomato stem/petiole with dense white fluffy/cottony mycelium spreading from it. This strongly suggests a white fungal mycelium disease. Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (white cotton-like mycelium on stems) or Southern_Blight (white cottony mycelium at soil line with sclerotia).

Let me view one reference image for Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot to confirm.

The reference image shows Sclerotinia with a bleached/hardened stem and hard black sclerotia at the soil line — somewhat different from the test image which shows a green stem/petiole with actively spreading fluffy white mycelium.

However, the symptom description for Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot explicitly mentions "white cotton-like mycelium" covering infected stem tissue, which matches the test image very closely. The test image appears to show active mycelial growth at an earlier stage before stem bleaching and sclerotia formation. Southern_Blight would show spherical sclerotia visible in the white mat, which aren't evident here.
